text: Subblocks (formerly Flashblocks) are partial blocks that the Ink sequencer streams while it is still building the full block, roughly every 200 ms. They let your application see a transaction’s outcome as a pre-confirmation, before the block is sealed.

A pre-confirmation carries the sequencer’s trust assumption, not the protocol’s. It can be revoked under the same conditions that allow the sequencer to reorg unsafe blocks. In streamed payloads, state_root and block_hash are always zero, so do not treat them as authoritative.
* Security : Sequencer-level security to protect users from malicious intents and exploits.
Ink is an OP Chain (Ethereum Layer 2) which is part of the Superchain.
Configuration options for OP Chains Enables OP Chains to configure their data availability provider, sequencer address, etc.
